title: Functions, Modules, and Types
learning_outcomes: Describe the purpose of functions, modules, and types and explain at least one listed subtopic.

Identify one validation, compatibility, security, or troubleshooting consideration relevant to the example.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will explore functions, modules, and types within XQuery. You will connect its syllabus topics to an inspectable example, check the expected result, and note tool/version limits.
content.why_it_matters: Functions, Modules, and Types matters because XML workflows rely on explicit structure and predictable processing. The lesson helps you reason about built-in functions, avoid a common misunderstanding, and make a result reproducible for another developer.

content_blocks.title: Functions, Modules, and Types: concept map

content_blocks.caption: The visual introduces functions, modules, and types; inspect the worked example and then verify it.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: XQuery extends XPath with expressions for constructing results and querying one or more XML sources. FLWOR expressions bind values, optionally filter and order them, and then return results.

content_blocks.title: Connect the subtopics
content_blocks.text: This lesson explicitly covers: Built-in functions; User-defined functions; Module imports; Type checking; Reusable query logic. Treat these as connected parts of one workflow: define the structure, make the relevant assumptions explicit, and verify a result with a small known input.

content_blocks.title: Inspectable example: Functions, Modules, and Types
content_blocks.code:
for $p in doc("catalog.xml")/catalog/product
where xs:decimal($p/price) gt 10
order by xs:decimal($p/price)
return $p/name
content_blocks.expected_output: An XQuery 3.1 processor returns product-name elements for products priced above 10, in ascending price order.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Inspect this example as text. Run it only in a processor that supports the shown language/version; the standard CodeLeaf playground previews HTML/CSS/JavaScript only and does not execute XML, XSD, XPath, XSLT, XQuery, Python, or SQL. Use an XQuery processor or compatible XML database, specify the query version, and test empty sequences, duplicates, data-type conversions, and namespace handling before relying on a result in an application.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the sample to its exact starting state before each experiment. Change one element, attribute, expression, or constraint at a time, then compare the result with the expected behavior.
content_blocks.limitations: Run with an XQuery processor or XML database that supports the syntax used. A browser preview does not execute XQuery.

content_blocks.title: Version and safety checkpoint
content_blocks.text: Record the exact processor and version: specification support is not universal, especially for XSD 1.1, XPath 2.0/3.1, XQuery, and XSLT 2.0/3.0.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Create a small synthetic example that demonstrates “Built-in functions”. Then add one boundary case involving “User-defined functions”. Write down what should happen before testing, and record the exact output or processor message afterward.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming a document is correct because it looks readable.
common_mistakes.why: Visual appearance does not prove well-formedness, schema validity, correct namespace handling, or application-level meaning.
common_mistakes.fix: Parse and validate the document with the intended processor, then assert its meaning using a focused test.

common_mistakes.problem: Mixing specification features with processor support.
common_mistakes.why: A standard may define features that a specific runtime does not implement.
common_mistakes.fix: Record the version and feature support; test with the actual target processor.

common_mistakes.why: Missing values, wrong types, namespace differences, or boundary inputs can expose failures.
common_mistakes.fix: Add a valid case, an invalid case, and an edge case to the verification notes.
